body:
## Summary

When any existing item row in a bank has a sealed body that fails AEAD authentication (for example one flipped character inside `items.content_ciphertext`), every new `remember`/`store` write to that bank fails with `factor_unavailable: content decryption failed`, even though the new write does not touch the unreadable row. The admission novelty factor appears to decrypt neighbor rows and propagates the decrypt error instead of skipping the unreadable row.

Found incidentally while verifying a separate read-listing fix; not fixed in that change.

## Reproduction

1. Create a data dir and store one item:

   ```
   CLIO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/repro clio remember "tamper probe note" --category task_spec --bank demo --actor agent --output json
   # ok
   ```

2. Copy the data dir. In the copy, open `clio.db` and flip one character inside the `ciphertext_b64` value of the stored `items.content_ciphertext` envelope (keeping base64 validity so the envelope still parses; this breaks AEAD authentication).

3. On the tampered copy:

   ```
   CLIO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/repro-copy target/debug/clio remember "write probe after corruption" \
     --category task_spec --bank demo --actor agent --output json
   {"code":"factor_unavailable","message":"factor_unavailable: content decryption failed","ok":false}  # exit 1
   ```

4. Control: the same `remember` command against the untouched copy succeeds (`ok: true`, exit 0).

Also reproduced in-process: with a file-backed database opened under a fresh key store, `store` for a new item fails with `factor_unavailable: no DEK for subject `<another subject>`' while an old sealed row is unreadable.

## Expected result

A write whose own inputs are valid should succeed (or report a targeted, self-explanatory failure). An unreadable neighbor row should at most degrade that item's novelty contribution (or skip it with a warning), not fail every write in the bank. Direct reads of the unreadable item (`clio get <id>`) correctly still report `forbidden: content decryption failed`; the listing tool (`clio inspect`) already skips unreadable rows.

## Actual result

Any create against the bank exits 1 with `{"code":"factor_unavailable","message":"factor_unavailable: content decryption failed","ok":false}`. A data dir with a single corrupted (or key-mismatched) row becomes write-hostile for the whole bank.

## Impact

One damaged or key-orphaned row blocks all ingestion into the affected bank, which is worse than the read side (listing still works, single reads still report the row's own error). No data loss occurs, but recovery requires repairing or removing the unreadable row first.

## Notes

- Error surfaced from the store decrypt layer (`clio-store` KMS decrypt maps AEAD authentication failure to `ErrorCode::Forbidden`, message `content decryption failed`), wrapped as `factor_unavailable` by the admission factor path (see `clio-admission` novelty scoring / `clio-mcp` write tools).
- The behavior is present on the current master build (`make compile`, `cargo test --workspace` green apart from this scenario).

comments.body:
## Partially fixed on master; the remaining cases are fixed here

Reproduced first, then fixed. The report was accurate about the symptom, but master already covered two of the seven ways a row can become unreadable, so the failure it describes no longer reproduces on the current build. The other five did.

### What master already handled

`StoreSignals::readable_neighbor` skipped a neighbor row only when the error code was `Forbidden` or `ErasedSubject`. That covers the two cases in this report — an AEAD-flip and a missing DEK:

```
CLIO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/repro-copy clio remember "write probe after corruption" --category task_spec --bank demo --actor agent --output json
  → exit 0, ok:true          (before this change)
```

### What still failed, and reproduced on master

All of these blocked every new write in the bank, each verified against a real `clio` binary and a real data dir:

| Damaged row | Result on master |
|---|---|
| `ciphertext_b64` not valid base64 | `factor_unavailable: invalid ciphertext encoding`, exit 1 |
| `nonce_b64` not valid base64 | `factor_unavailable: invalid nonce encoding`, exit 1 |
| nonce of the wrong length | `factor_unavailable: invalid nonce length`, exit 1 |
| envelope JSON malformed | `factor_unavailable: ciphertext envelope decode failed: …`, exit 1 |
| `content_ciphertext` empty or NULL | `factor_unavailable: item row missing content_ciphertext`, exit 1 |

### Cause

Those five all reported `ErrorCode::Internal`, which `readable_neighbor` did not match. The same code is also what a genuinely broken backend reports (`map_db_err` in `crates/clio-store/src/migrate.rs:19`, including an unreadable key-store file from `KmsDb::get`), so widening the skip to `Internal` would have silently admitted writes and reads while the store was actually down. The condition had no code of its own, which is why it was shared.

### Fix

- `crates/clio-types/src/error.rs` — new `ErrorCode::UnreadableContent` and one shared predicate `AmError::is_unreadable_content()` (true for `UnreadableContent`, `Forbidden`, `ErasedSubject`; deliberately false for `Internal`).
- The content-read failures are tagged with it: `dek.rs` (envelope decode, nonce/ciphertext base64, nonce length), `content_envelope.rs` (sealed bytes that are not DualContent v1), `item_persist.rs` (`missing_ciphertext`, `content_format_mismatch`), and the two `get_item` backends for an empty content column.
- `crates/clio-mcp/src/runtime_sinks.rs` — `readable_neighbor` now uses the predicate, so one bad row costs only its own novelty contribution.
- `crates/clio-store/src/dek.rs` — the `DekProvider::decrypt` contract now states that implementations must keep content failures and key-store failures apart, so this cannot silently regress.

### Verified

New write into a bank that already holds one unreadable row, for all seven damage shapes, plus the undamaged control — all `exit=0, ok:true`. Log: `private/clio-private/logs/issue17-repro.log`.

The behaviour this report asked to preserve is intact: a direct read of the damaged row still reports its own error, now `{"code":"unreadable_content","message":"invalid ciphertext encoding","ok":false}` instead of the catch-all `internal`. `clio recall` returns the items that are readable.

Fail-closed is preserved and covered by a test: a neighbour whose key store fails still produces `factor_unavailable`, because `Internal` is not skippable (`runtime_sinks_content_tests.rs::backend_failure_still_fails_closed`). Against a genuinely unreadable database the CLI fails 6 runs out of 6 with exit 1 — log: `private/clio-private/logs/corrupt-db-write-honesty.log`.

`make check` exit 0 (53 suites). `make coverage`: 352 files, all at or above the 90% floor, TOTAL lines 97.90% / functions 98.73% (baseline 97.89% / 98.73%) — log: `private/clio-private/logs/make-coverage-summary.log`.

### Notes

- Six existing tests asserted the old code for these same conditions and were updated. Every one still fails closed; only the code string changed.
- The read side has the same hole and is **not** fixed here — see #33.
- `pg_lock::tests::a_second_holder_waits_until_the_first_releases` fails intermittently under workspace-parallel load and aborts the coverage gate before any report is produced. Pre-existing, unrelated, filed as #32.

title: One unreadable ciphertext row blocks all new writes to the bank with factor_unavailable during admission
